surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions for SiO2 and Al2O3 deposition involve self-limiting half-reactions where surface species react with gaseous precursors. For SiO2, the A half-reaction involves surface hydroxyls reacting with SiCl4 to form chlorinated surface species, while the B half-reaction involves the reaction of surface chlorinated species with H2O to regenerate hydroxyls. For Al2O3, the A half-reaction involves surface hydroxyls reacting with TMA to form methylated surface species, while the B half-reaction involves the reaction of surface methylated species with H2O to regenerate hydroxyls.
evidence: The text describes the surface reactions for SiO2 and Al2O3 deposition using the following equations: (A) Si-OH + SiCl4 -> Si-0-SiCl2 + HCl, (B) Si-Cl + H2O -> Si-OH + HCl for SiO2, and (A) Al-OH + Al(CH3)3 -> Al-O-Al(CH3)2 + CH4, (B) Al-CH3 + H2O -> Al-OH + CH4 for Al2O3. The surface species involved in these reactions include Si-Cl, Si-0-SiCl2, Al-CH3, and Al-O-Al(CH3)2.
